Off-plan guide

Buying off-plan in Morocco: risks, safeguards and essential checks

This guide helps buyers structure checks before committing. It does not replace a notary, lawyer, technical expert or financial adviser.

Why buyers should slow down before signing

A property project can look clear in a brochure while important documents remain incomplete. The decision should connect price, file, developer, payments, timeline and real intended use.

What to verify

The method is to request documents, understand unclear points and have binding commitments reviewed by qualified professionals when the purchase becomes serious.

  • Identity of the seller or developer.
  • Title deed, plans, surfaces and shared authorizations.
  • Payment schedule, recipient and exit conditions.
  • Delivery, guarantees, reservations and post-signature follow-up.

The role of S.A.F.E

S.A.F.E helps organize the first layer of analysis. The framework creates no legal guarantee and never replaces professional checks.

Checklist before deciding

  • Identify the operator and responsible contacts.
  • Compare price with neighborhood and quality.
  • Request useful documents early.
  • Understand every payment before transferring funds.
  • Have binding documents reviewed.
  • Allow margin for timing and budget changes.
This article is editorial analysis and does not constitute legal, tax, financial or notarial advice.

FAQ

Is this guide legal advice?

No. It is editorial analysis designed to help buyers ask the right questions.

Does S.A.F.E replace a notary?

No. S.A.F.E never replaces notarial, legal, tax, financial or technical checks.

What if a document is missing?

Slow down, request written clarification and consult a professional if the commitment is significant.
